name: Kaminarimon after dark
short_description: Photograph Senso-ji's Thunder Gate and giant lantern from the public approach after the evening lights come on.

shooting_area.name: Public approach south of Kaminarimon
shooting_area.standing_instruction: Stay on the public pedestrian approach south of the gate. Keep clear of the road, gate threshold, worshippers, queues and moving foot traffic.
shooting_area.verification_note: The area is estimated from public map context and the reference composition. It has not been checked on site.

shot_guide.bearing_method: calculated from the approximate public approach to the landmark coordinate
shot_guide.phone_camera_suggestion: Start with the main 1x camera. Move only within the public approach and wait for a natural gap rather than backing into the road.
shot_guide.composition_instruction: Center the lantern, keep the roofline level and include enough of both gate pillars to show the full entrance without cutting into pedestrian flow.
shot_guide.composition_short_instruction: Center the lantern and keep both red gate pillars balanced.
shot_guide.expected_view: The illuminated red gate and lantern filling the frame from the public approach.
field_checks_needed: Confirm the practical standing area without blocking pedestrians.
Measure the final bearing and focal length.
Confirm current lighting and photography signs.
Check whether temporary queues or event controls change the approach.

timing_and_light.primary_recommendation: Try blue hour into early evening, when the gate lighting can separate the red structure from the sky. Lighting timing is not confirmed.
timing_and_light.alternate_recommendation: Early morning may reduce pedestrian density, but the illuminated-night appearance will be different.
timing_and_light.lighting_direction_note: The camera faces almost north, so the sky behind the gate is indirect sunset light rather than a direct sunset view.
timing_and_light.subject_lighting_note: No current official English lighting schedule was found for Kaminarimon. Treat illumination as variable.

access.line: Tokyo Metro Ginza Line / Toei Asakusa Line / Tobu Skytree Line
access.cost_note: No fee is presented for the public gate approach. Confirm any separately ticketed facilities before visiting.
access.published_hours: The official English Senso-ji page identifies the site and address but does not clearly publish hours for this outdoor composition.

accessibility.summary: A step-free route to the exact recommended area has not been confirmed.
accessibility.note: Use current station and on-site accessibility information.

conditions.crowd_note: Senso-ji is a major place of worship and visitor destination. Crowd density varies strongly by event and time; this rating is an editorial estimate.
conditions.safety_note: Do not step into Kaminarimon-dori, walk backward into others or stop in the gate threshold while composing.

rules_and_respect.site_type: active Buddhist temple entrance and public approach
guidance: Worship and pedestrian movement take priority over photography.
Follow every posted sign and staff instruction.
Do not photograph identifiable worshippers without permission.
Do not block the gate threshold, queues, shops or the public road.
Avoid tripods unless current rules clearly permit them and they do not obstruct anyone.
Keep voices, flashes and screen brightness restrained at night.
rules_and_respect.editorial_rule: ViewRoam must not state that tripods or commercial shoots are permitted without current site confirmation.

live_conditions.title: Photography rules need an on-site check
live_conditions.message: The official English sources reviewed do not publish a complete photography or tripod policy. Follow current signs and staff instructions.

seasonal_notes.note: Seasonal events can significantly increase crowding and change pedestrian controls.
Blue hour is later; allow for heat, humidity and evening events.
Clearer evenings may improve color and architectural detail.
Earlier darkness can make the illuminated composition easier to include in an evening route.
